note: Two owner-chosen pilot cases from the 18 November 2026 source pack. Official records do not print event lat/lon. Map areas are named sites only, not event fixes. The app does not add precision the sources do not give.

cases.title: The Puerto Rico Object
cases.place_label: Rafael Hernandez Airport, near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico
cases.place_as_written: A U.S. Customs and Border Protection aircraft “flying above Rafael Hernandez Airport near Aguadilla, Puerto Rico.” The IR sensor “first detected the objects near the northeastern side of the airport” and “lost contact with them over the airport’s central parking apron.” The report states that a reconstruction “demonstrates that the objects remained over land during the encounter.”
cases.time_notes: The AARO report also states that “sunset occurred at 7:48 p.m. local time.” Footnote 5 (www.sunrisesunset.com) is attached after the sentence that contains both figures, so it is [UNKNOWN] from the report’s layout alone whether the 9:22 p.m. figure is sensor metadata, the cited site, or both. The report does not spell out a named time zone beyond “local time.”
cases.summary: AARO’s report states that on April 26, 2013 an infrared sensor on a CBP aircraft captured thermal video of objects over Rafael Hernandez Airport that “appeared to move at a high rate of speed,” appeared to separate, and “seemed to enter, exit, and disappear into the Atlantic Ocean off Puerto Rico’s northwestern coast.” AARO assesses with high confidence that the objects did not exhibit anomalous speeds or transmedium behavior, that the video shows two objects traveling near each other rather than one object splitting, and that they remained over land; it assesses with moderate confidence that they were a pair of sky lanterns. The report itself notes that “the video’s poor quality reduces AARO’s confidence in categorically identifying the objects.”
cases.official_status: Officially confirmed (that the record exists): AARO published a case-resolution report stating that CBP infrared footage was recorded on April 26, 2013 above Rafael Hernandez Airport. Analytic conclusions in that report are AARO’s assessments, not a separately confirmed identification.

cases.title: Rendlesham Forest / RAF Woodbridge
cases.place_label: Back gate at RAF Woodbridge, and Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk
cases.place_as_written: “unusual lights outside the back gate at RAF Woodbridge”; a “strange glowing object in the forest”; later “near the back gate”; then “the area” where depressions were found. The UK National Archives collection page places the events at “a Royal Air Force (RAF) base in Suffolk,” names RAF Woodbridge, and says servicemen “investigated an area of Rendlesham Forest on two separate nights.”
cases.date_as_printed: Memorandum date: 13 Jan 81. First reported observation: “Early in the morning of 27 Dec 80 (approximately 0300L).” Radiation check: “The following night (29 Dec 80).”
cases.time_as_printed: Approximately 0300L on 27 Dec 80; no clock time given for 29 Dec 80; paragraph 3 begins “Later in the night.”
cases.time_notes: The memorandum does not further define the “L” suffix. Zone beyond that suffix: [UNKNOWN]. The “next day” depressions are not given a numbered calendar date. Clock time for the 29 Dec 80 radiation check: [UNKNOWN]. Paragraph 3 follows the 29 Dec 80 sentence but does not explicitly re-date itself; clock time for paragraph 3: [UNKNOWN].
cases.summary: Lt Col Halt, Deputy Base Commander, 81st Combat Support Group, reported that early on 27 Dec 80 (approximately 0300L) USAF security police at the back gate of RAF Woodbridge saw unusual lights and then described a “metalic” (spelling as written), triangular glowing object in the forest, later briefly seen again near the back gate; the next day, depressions were found at the site. On the night of 29 Dec 80 the area was checked for radiation, and “later in the night” Halt, who writes that he was among the witnesses to the activities in paragraphs 2 and 3, described a red sun-like light in the trees and then star-like objects to the north and south.
cases.official_status: Officially confirmed (that the report exists): The UK National Archives holds the Ministry of Defence file and presents the Halt memorandum as the “single sheet report” that is “the only record of the event itself” in its holdings. A 16 October 2001 House of Lords written answer stated that this was the only USAF material held by the MoD on the incident, that MoD records from the same period “document no evidence of unusual radar returns,” and that there was “no indication from the papers held on file that MoD raised any further questions with Lieutenant Colonel Halt following receipt of his memorandum in 1981.” The National Archives collection page says a note in response to a Parliamentary Question “confirmed that there was nothing of defence interest in the alleged sighting.”

areas.name: MOD Woodbridge (Rock Barracks)
areas.note: OSM maps the current military site under this name. A feature named “RAF Woodbridge” was not found in OpenStreetMap in the extract taken on 18 November 2026. This outline is not a 1980 base boundary and is not an event fix.

cases.precision_label: Named site location from OpenStreetMap, not an event fix
cases.precision_note: The official record names the back gate at RAF Woodbridge and an area of Rendlesham Forest, but does not print coordinates. Official gazetteer coordinates were not retrieved in the source pack. The shaded outlines are the OpenStreetMap features for Rendlesham Forest and for MOD Woodbridge (Rock Barracks). No OpenStreetMap feature named “back gate” or “RAF Woodbridge” was found. An OSM tourism viewpoint named “Rendlesham East Gate” exists in the forest area; it is not used here as the official back-gate location, because the official record does not use that name and does not give coordinates.
